purpose: generic PRT operating assumptions so the configuration chain (person trips -> vehicle trips -> berths -> module -> footprint) can run end to end for the demonstration; every value is replaceable by an observed or specified value and is tagged as an assumption in every output
public_repository_note: generic values only; no supplier-specific operating data

C01_average_party_size_pax_per_vehicle_t.statement: average occupancy of a PRT vehicle trip in the commute peak; commuters mostly travel alone
C01_average_party_size_pax_per_vehicle_t.reference: vehicle occupancy for commuting is typically 1.1-1.5; the maximum capacity (6) is never used as the load

C02_berth_cycle_s.statement: one berth cycle = vehicle entry, alighting, boarding, exit
C02_berth_cycle_s.reference: order of magnitude for offline PRT berths; not measured

C03_berth_utilization_max.statement: design margin: a berth is sized for at most 80 % of its theoretical cycle throughput

C04_within_hour_peaking_factor.statement: peak-15-minute flow x 4 divided by the hourly flow; applied to berth sizing ONLY, never to the demand chain (it is not a second peak-hour share)

C05_min_guideway_headway_s.statement: minimum operating headway between vehicles on the guideway; lane throughput = 3600 / headway

C06_site_footprint_available.statement: the selected module's footprint is assumed to be constructible at every station; the per-station constructible space has NOT been acquired, so this assumption stands in for it

C07_no_separate_staging_berths.statement: the drawings show no staging berths; empty vehicles are assumed to be supplied from the guideway as needed
